8. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:18305 3 CRA-12478-2025 through the record as per the prosecution story complainant i.e. father of the victim lodged a report at Police Station Shahganj that on 23.10.2021 that his daughter victim had gone missing after he left his home at about 08.00 a.m. When he returned back from his field at about 07.00 p.m. then he found that his daughter was not present.
On enquiry it was revealed that she had gone to her school at 11.00 a.m. but did not return in the evening though usually she used to return by 05.00 p.m.

She was searched for in the neighbourhood and at the place of relatives but when she could not be traced, then FIR was registered at Police Station Shahganj registering case Crime No.440/2021 under Section 363 of IPC.

Her statements under Section 164 were recorded.
On the basis of her case diary statement and statements given to the Magistrate, sections 343, 376(3) of IPC and Section 5 r/w. 6 of POCSO Act were added.
Victim was subjected to medical examination.
Her school records were seized.

Necessary forensic tests were conducted and after investigation,
charge- sheet was filed.
On 22.12.2021, when trial was conducted and appellant has been convicted as above.

sentences.text: She had visited Rajan at Bhopal with whom she had met one-two years prior to the incident in her own village.
They were friends and later on developed love for each other.
She stated that she wanted to marry to him.
On 23rd October, there was an altercation with family members on account of her plans to marry Rajan.
In her 164 statements, victim stated that she stayed with Rajan for two days.
Rajan had not committed any wrong.
She wanted to live with Rajan and wants to perform marriage with Rajan.
11. Contrary statements have been given as case diary statements recorded by the police as contained in Ex.P/5.

Date of recording of 164 statement is 27.10.2021 whereas 161 statement were recorded on 25.10.2021.
12.
In Ex.P/10C i.e. Scholar Register, date of birth of the victim is mentioned as 18.08.2006.
It is mentioned that she had taken admission in Class First on 11.07.2012 and had left the school on 17.06.2017.
Age of Rajan has come on record to be 23 years.
13. As per FSL report Ex.P/23
human sperms
were found on Article A,B and C i.e. slide, underwear of the victim and slide of the accused Rajendra @ Raja.
DNA report Ex.P/28A reveals that Y-DNA profile obtained from the vaginal slide of the victim and underwear of the victim matched with the blood sample of the accused Rajan.
14. Father of the victim (PW-1) supported the prosecution case.
In cross-examination, he admitted that he does not know date of birth of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18305 5 CRA-12478-2025 the victim.
He does not know date of birth of any of his children.
He admits in para-5 of his cross-examination that date of birth of the victim has given on the basis of estimation.
He stated that he does not know his own date of marriage.
In para-7, this witness that he had not produced any birth certificate from any hospital or a certificate issued by Kotwar.
He admits that he had not given any document in relation to date of birth of the victim.
15. (PW-2) is the victim.
She stated that she was student of 12th class.
She has stated in her examination-in-chief what she had stated before the learned Magistrate in her 164 statements.
She was declared hostile.
Leading question were put her but she did not support the prosecution case.
In para-7 of her cross-examination, victim stated that at the time when she had left her home, she was an adult and aged about 19 years.
Since her parents wanted to marry her somewhere else, she has left her home out of anger.
She stated that accused never committed any wrong and had never lured her in the name of marriage.
16. (PW-3) is mother of the victim.
She too was declared hostile and leading questions were put her.
In para-10 of her cross-examination, she stated that she has four children and victim is the eldest child.
She admits that she does not remember date of birth of any of her four children.
She admits that even she does not member her own date of birth.

17. Anita Ahirwar (PW-4) stated that she was posted at Primary NEUTRAL CITATION NO.

She had give documents showing date of birth of the victim to be 28.08.2006.

sentences.text: An entry is made in the school register as to on what basis of date of birth is recorded.
She admits that it is not mentioned in the Scholar Register as to on what basis date of birth was recorded.
18. Dr. Rashi Tiwari (PW-5) had conducted the MLC on the victim.
This doctor stated that there were no external or internal injury marks on the body.
Hymen of the victim was ruptured but no definite opinion could be given in regard to violation of privacy.
In cross- examination doctor admits that no documents were seen by her in regard to age of the victim.
In para-8 of her cross-examination, she stated that organs of the victim were under development and not fully developed, therefore, her age was less than 17 years.
19. When all these facts are taken into consideration then admittedly in view of Scholar Register date of birth of victim is 28.08.2006.
Victim was minor at the time of the incident.
It is true that teen age infatuation often results in relationship.
It is also true that victim performed marriage with the accused for whom she had love and affection.
She is 08 months pregnant and is about to deliver a child.

11. However, it is also true that the power which can be NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:18305 7 CRA-12478-2025 exercised by the Hon'ble the Supreme Court under Article 142 of the Constitution of India is not available to the High Courts.

All the three judgments namely Right to Privacy of Adolescents, K. Dhandapani and K. Kirubakaran (supra) are those where Hon'ble the Supreme Court decided to exercise its authority under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.

12. Since that authority is not available to us and there is clear record of date of birth of the victim to be 28.08.2006, which shows that she was about 15 years and 2 months on the date of the incident.
We are unable to show indulgence despite having sympathy for the appellant.
Accordingly, taking this fact into consideration that sympathy cannot take place alone and substitute the legal proof, we are unable to extend any help.
13. Thus, the appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
